IE’27 Workshop · Skopje, North Macedonia · Hybrid

Future-Proofing the Intelligent Environments Workforce

Skills, Learning and Assessment in the Age of Generative AI

What capabilities should future Intelligent Environments professionals develop when AI can perform an increasing share of routine cognitive work — and how do we know students have actually developed them?
Call for Contributions Important Dates

Why SKILLS4IE?

Artificial intelligence is changing not only the systems we build, but also how future engineers and computing professionals learn, work, and demonstrate expertise.

Advances in artificial intelligence, cyber-physical systems, IoT, edge computing and digital twins are transforming intelligent environments and the skills needed to develop them. At the same time, AI is changing how future professionals learn, work and demonstrate expertise.

Skills4IE’27 connects three perspectives: the technical and transversal competencies required by future professionals; approaches to learning in computing and engineering education; and credible assessment in the age of generative AI.

The workshop brings together researchers, educators and industry practitioners to examine systems reasoning, human–AI collaboration, critical evaluation, verification and responsible decision-making, and to identify practical directions for curricula, learning and assessment.

Core question

What should students still be able to do independently, and what should they learn to do effectively together with AI?

The goal is not AI avoidance. It is credible preparation for intelligent, responsible professional practice.

Workshop themes

SKILLS4IE connects the capabilities we want graduates to have with the educational experiences that develop them and the evidence that demonstrates competence.

1

Future Skills

What should graduates know and be able to do in an AI-rich professional environment?

  • Systems thinking and problem formulation
  • Design, diagnosis and troubleshooting
  • Transfer to unfamiliar situations
  • Critical evaluation of AI-generated solutions
  • Responsible and trustworthy AI practice
  • Human–AI collaboration and professional judgement
2

Learning & Curriculum

How should we design learning experiences that develop higher-order expertise?

  • Authentic and challenge-based learning
  • Project- and problem-based education
  • Labs, simulations and digital twins
  • AI as tutor, critic, collaborator or development tool
  • Verification and critique of AI output
  • Curriculum redesign for future practice
3

Assessment

What constitutes convincing evidence of learning when AI assistance is readily available?

  • Authentic and performance-based assessment
  • Reasoning rather than reproduction
  • Transfer to unfamiliar problems
  • Assessment with and without AI
  • Process-based evidence of learning
  • Validity, reliability, fairness and scalability
Competencies we want graduates to develop
→
Learning experiences that can develop them
→
Assessment evidence that can credibly demonstrate them

Call for Contributions

We welcome contributions on future-ready skills, learning and assessment, including research results, ongoing work, educational experiences and position-oriented contributions.

Relevant contributions may include:

  • Empirical studies of learning or assessment
  • Innovative course or curriculum designs
  • Assessment redesign in response to Generative AI
  • Educational uses of AI and intelligent learning environments
  • Competency frameworks for future computing and engineering professionals
  • Industrial perspectives on changing skill requirements
  • Institutional or programme-level educational transformation
  • Lessons from successful or unsuccessful interventions
  • Conceptual or position papers challenging current educational assumptions

Especially encouraged

Contributions that connect at least two of the workshop’s three dimensions:

Skills · Learning · Assessment

You do not need to be an education researcher to contribute. Technical course, programme, laboratory and industrial-training experiences are particularly welcome.

ResearchOngoing workEducational practiceIndustry perspectivesPosition contributions

Who should participate?

A cross-disciplinary community interested in how intelligent technologies are reshaping professional competence and technical education.

Intelligent Environments

Researchers in AI, IoT, cyber-physical systems, distributed systems, digital twins, sensing and human-centred computing.

Education & Assessment

Computing and engineering educators, educational researchers, curriculum designers and researchers in AI and education.

Industry & Future Workforce

Industry professionals, workforce-development specialists, doctoral researchers and early-career academics.

Workshop format

SKILLS4IE’27 is designed as an interactive workshop combining selected contributions with structured discussion and collaborative activities. IE’27 schedules workshops during the first two days of the conference; the exact SKILLS4IE’27 session date and time will be announced when the programme is finalised.

Alongside paper presentations, participants will work across disciplinary boundaries to connect individual experiences and evidence. The workshop will culminate in a collective discussion around three questions:

  • What should we teach?
  • How should students learn it?
  • What evidence would convince us that they can actually do it?

Workshop outcome

Participants will contribute to an evolving SKILLS4IE competency–learning–assessment map for Intelligent Environments education.

The ambition is a reusable framework that can support curriculum and assessment design across computing, engineering and related disciplines.
